source.title: Getting started with AI Alignment research: how to reproduce an experiment from research paper

record.file_problem: Full post is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The author reports results from running the weak-to-strong experiments, including weak-label fine-tuning and accuracy comparisons, as a reproduction of the original method.
record.gate_note: The post reports results from a small GPT-2 experiment and one vision experiment. The larger GPT-2/Qwen sweep is presented as an instruction; no results from that sweep are reported. No PGR values are calculated.
record.test_reason: The author reruns the original paper's code (sweep.py, run_weak_strong.py) on the same tasks and reports weak, strong-ceiling and weak-to-strong accuracies. These numbers allow PGR to be computed for one GPT-2 pair and one vision pair. The evidence is a single run per pair with no uncertainty estimates.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The post is a how-to guide: the author reports the accuracies obtained and presents successful runs as a working setup for beginners. The author draws no evaluative conclusion beyond restating the paper's claim that strong models can surpass their weak supervisors.
record.recipe_differences: Reports running the original weak-to-strong scripts with package fixes and gives instructions for a small GPT-2 run and a vision run; the larger sweep is described but has no reported results.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported results differ between the GPT-2 supervisor/student settings and the vision setting; no controlled sensitivity sweep is reported.
record.problems: The reported GPT-2 and vision results have no uncertainty estimates or reported controls. The GPT-2 results are a small set of model combinations; the larger sweep is not reported. PGR is not calculated.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result rows omitted. The post describes a larger sweep and a resulting plot, but gives no measurements from that run.

untested.parts: Only one weak/strong pair per modality, each run once. No NLP task beyond the sweep's default dataset, and no chess or reward modelling.

Not tested. Each modality has a single supervisor/student pair, so no variation with size, task or representations is shown. The larger GPT-2/Qwen sweep is given only as an instruction, with no results reported.

record.verdict_notes: This is a tutorial blog post, not a study. The record's V1 'challenges' label, built on r5, has been removed: r5 and r3 are same-size self-training runs. The record's 'limits_scope' labels for students staying below the strong ceiling have also been removed: PGR below 1 is consistent with V1, which only requires PGR above 0. The vision setup copies the original paper's own vision experiment, so it replicates that result rather than extending it.

versions.untested_parts: PGR is not calculated; only the reported accuracies can be compared. The reported experiments cover the stated GPT-2 settings and one vision setting.
Auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, and loss variants.
Only small GPT-2 settings and one vision setting have reported results. No reported results for chess, reward modelling, representations, or the proposed larger GPT-2/Qwen sweep.
Distribution shift, exploiting supervisor limitations, and shared errors.
Only the stated AlexNet-to-Dino-ResNet50 vision experiment.
